props.title: Spot a Phishing Email
props.sub: Five red flags in two minutes

narration.text: Welcome. In the next few minutes you'll learn to spot a phishing email before it costs you.

claims.text: Phishing emails try to trick people into clicking, paying or sharing data.

narration.text: Most attacks on companies start with a single email. ^ It looks routine, it feels urgent, and it only needs one click.

claims.text: Phishing email is the most common way attacks reach our staff.

props.def: A fake message that pretends to be someone you trust, to make you click, pay or share data.
props.note: It can arrive by email, text, phone or chat.

narration.text: ^ Phishing is a fake message that pretends to come from someone you trust. ^ And it isn't only email: texts, calls and chat messages count too.

claims.text: Phishing impersonates a trusted sender to obtain clicks, payments or data.
Phishing also arrives by SMS, voice and chat.

narration.text: Here's how it unfolds. ^ The bait: an urgent email. ^ The hook: a link or an attachment. ^ The catch: a fake login page takes your password. ^ And then the damage: account takeover or malware.

claims.text: Typical phishing flow: email, link, credential page, account takeover.

email.subject: URGENT: Your mailbox will be closed today
body: Your mailbox exceeded its limit and will be closed in 2 hours.
Click below to keep your account active.

narration.text: Let's check a real-looking example. ^ First, the sender's domain: northwlnd, with an L instead of an I.
^ Second, a generic greeting instead of your name. ^ Third, pressure: closed in two hours.
^ And finally, the button. Hover over it first and check where it really goes.

claims.text: Look-alike domains, generic greetings, urgency and disguised links are phishing red flags.

scenes.visual: Mock email from a look-alike domain with four orange callouts

narration.text: A few more signs to pause for: ^ an attachment you didn't expect, ^ any request for a password or a code, ^ and any change to payment or bank details.

claims.text: Unexpected attachments, credential requests and payment changes are red flags.

props.title: What to do
dont: Reply to ask if it's real
do: Verify using a contact you already know

narration.text: So what do you do? ^ Don't click the link, ^ and don't reply to ask if it's real. ^ Instead, verify using a contact you already know, ^ and press the Report Phishing button.

claims.text: Staff must report suspicious email with the Report Phishing button.

props.q: An urgent email asks you to log in to keep your mailbox. What do you do?
options: Report it, then check via the known portal
props.why: Never use the email's own link; report it and verify independently.

narration.text: Quick check. An urgent email asks you to log in to keep your mailbox. What do you do?
^ The answer is C. Report it, then check through the portal you already know.
Let's recap. ^ Check the domain. ^ Distrust urgency. ^ Hover before you click. ^ And report, don't reply.

claims.text: Recap of red flags and reporting.
